4] Counsel for the appellant has submitted that a perusal of the deposition of the prosecutrix PW-4 clearly reveals that she was a consenting party as she had accompanied the appellant to his sister's house at Gram Khokari on the motorcycle and from there she was taken to his Aunt's house, and from there, while he was taking her to the Court for NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:27956 CRA No.3394-2021 marriage, after seeing her mother and father, she ran to them only.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the prosecutrix has admitted that she has resided with the appellant at Gram Khokari for around four days, whereas at Gram Petlawad in his Aunt's house, for around 8 days.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: She has also been suggested that the appellant used to work with her as labour and she used to talk to him on mobile, to which she has denied, and she has also been suggested that as her mother used to beat her, hence, she had run away with the appellant.

sentences.text: She has also stated that in her family around 10 to 15 persons reside together.

sentences.text: 6] Counsel has also submitted that the age of the prosecutrix has not been proved beyond reasonable doubt to be less than 16 years, as in proof of her age, only her progress card and scholar register have been filed, and there is nothing on record to positively establish her age to be less than 16 years.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: Counsel has also submitted that the FSL report Ex.D/16 is also negative and is in favour of the appellant.

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that the appeal be allowed, and the appellant be acquitted.

sentences.text: 7] Counsel for the State has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for interference is made out.

sentences.text: 8] Heard.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the record, it is found that the prosecutrix went missing from her home on 22.02.2018, and she has been recovered vide recovery memo Ex.P/3 on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:27956 CRA No.3394-2021 09.03.2018.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: Thus, apparently, the prosecutrix was away from home for a period of around 16 days.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text:
So far as her age is concerned, it is found that her date of birth is stated to be 02.04.2004, which is proved through her Scholar Register Ex.P/2C as also her progress card report Ex.P/3, which have been proved by PW-1 Devi Singh Thakur, Principal of Government Girls Middle, School, Ujjain, who has also admitted that the entries have not been carried out by him, and her date of birth has been entered into the scholar register after seeing her primary school mark sheet, of Primary School,
Tilgara.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: Whereas, the parents of the prosecutrix, PW-2 and PW-3 have also stated that they had mentioned the date of birth of their daughter by their guesstimate only as they did not remember her exact date of birth.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: In such circumstances, coupled with the fact that PW-6 Dr. Neena Bhawsar has also found that the secondary sexual characters of the prosecutrix were fully developed, this Court is of the considered opinion that the prosecution has not been able to prove the age of the prosecutrix to be less than 18 years beyond reasonable doubt.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text:
9] So far as the forceful sexual intercourse of the prosecutrix is concerned, it is found that PW-6 Dr.
Neena Bhawsar has not found any external or internal injury suffered by the prosecutrix and,
although her hymen was ruptured, but there was no bleeding found along with her private part.
From the deposition of the prosecutrix-PW-4, it is found that she had accompanied the appellant and co-accused Javarsingh on a motorcycle, and she has not raised any alarm while she resided with the appellant for around 16 days.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: She has also denied that the appellant used NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:27956 CRA No.3394-2021 to work with her father as labour, although she has also admitted that in para 18 of her cross-examination that the places where she resided with the appellant were full of women and other persons, including children, and has also stated that when she had gone to Petlawad, she had prepared food for herself and for the appellant, whereas at village Khokari, food was cooked by the sister of the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: She has also admitted that she used to eat along with sister of the appellant and his family members.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: She has also admitted that she was taken by the appellant and the co-accused Javarsingh in a bus to Badnawar and at Petlawad in the house of the appellant's Aunt, which was of one room only, and they used to sleep and eat together in the same room.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: She has also admitted in her cross- examination that the houses in which she has resided with the appellant had neighboring houses also, but she did not inform any person that she has been abducted by the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: She has also admitted in para 28 of her cross-examination that she did not want to reside with her parents, hence, she had left her house.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

10] In such facts and circumstances, with the aforesaid evidence adduced by the defence on record,
this Court has no hesitation to hold that the prosecutrix was a consenting party.
sentences._hearing_file: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text:
In view of the same,
this Court is of the considered opinion that the prosecution has not been able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

sentences.text: 11] Accordingly, the impugned judgement of conviction dated 20.01.2021, cannot be sustained in the eyes of law, and the same is hereby NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:27956 CRA No.3394-2021 set aside and the appellantis hereby acquitted.

sentences.text: Appellant is lodged in jail, he be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.

sentences.text: 12] With the aforesaid, the appeal stands allowed and disposed of.

opennyai_summary.10_January_2025__arguments:
It is a case of consensual relation.
The victim eloped with the applicant at her own.
No offence, as alleged, is committed by the applicant.
The consent of victim is immaterial in view of the fact that she was minor at the time of alleged incident.
Therefore, the applicant may not be extended benefit bail.
opennyai_summary.10_January_2025__ANALYSIS:
Heard rival submissions of both the parties and perused the record.
In view of the specific allegations of penetrative sexual assault with the minor victim against her will and the age difference of the victim and the accused, the gravity of alleged offence is prima facie made out.
The assault by knife is corroborated by the medical evidence.
In view of these aggravating factors and overall consideration of the factual scenario, this Court is of considered opinion that the applicant does not deserve to be released on bail.
